data.name: Nish
data.gender_notes: Nish is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Nish refers to the god of the night or the night itself. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'nisha', meaning 'protection' or 'defence'. Nish is believed to provide shelter and protection to all living beings during the night. The name Nish carries the meaning “Lord of the Night” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nish usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the night and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_sanskrit.name: निश
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The Sanskrit word निश (Nish) comes from the root नि (ni), which means 'to cover, to conceal, to hide'. The suffix श (sh) is a locative suffix, indicating a place or a state. So, निश (Nish) can be translated as 'the place of concealment', 'the state of obscurity', or 'the time of night'. It can also be interpreted as 'the absence of light' or 'the darkness'. This name is often used to denote the night, the darkness, or the obscurity in Hindu mythology and literature.

data.cultural_impact: The Hindu festival of Diwali, also known as the Festival of Lights, celebrates the return of Lord Rama from his exile and victory over the demon king Ravana. The festival is marked by the lighting of oil lamps and diyas, which symbolizes the victory of good over evil.
data.spiritual_significance: Diwali is also considered a time for spiritual growth and renewal and the coming year is auspicious to start new ventures or beginnings. It’s believed that Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, appears on this night and blesses her devotees with prosperity and good fortune.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nish signifies the 'End' or 'Goal' in life, representing the pursuit of enlightenment and self-realization towards the ultimate truth. The name encourages one to keep moving forward with determination and conviction, towards the infinite light of consciousness.
